topic.title: Toyota Built 450 Prototypes Before Anyone Heard of Lexus

title: Toyota vs Mercedes: The Car Built to Steal Its Buyers
description:
Why did Toyota secretly build a whole new luxury brand from scratch?
Lexus, 1984 to 1989, told from Toyota's own company history and the launch reports.
Sources: Toyota, Jalopnik, Motoring Research (Jul 2026).
Based on public records and reporting. Not financial or legal advice.

cta: Lexus or Mercedes: which badge would you park outside? Comment

lines.text: Toyota could sell a car to anyone, except the people who bought a Mercedes.
Its own best customers got richer, and traded up to Mercedes and BMW.
So in 1984, Toyota started a secret project: a luxury car to win them back.
Its engineers drove test cars more than 3.5M kilometres.
Jalopnik puts the bill at about $1B. So would a Mercedes buyer ever pay that kind of money for a Toyota?
Toyota left its own name off. Six years on, it opened Lexus in America, at $35,000 a car.
By the end of that year, Lexus had hit its forecast of 16,000 cars.
Behind that one car, Toyota had built about 450 prototypes, before anyone had heard the name Lexus.
Lexus or Mercedes: which badge would you park outside? Either way, the Lexus was built by Toyota.

note: 1 beats between the hook and the payoff open a new question; at least 2 ("But that's not where the dealer makes his money.", "So why would he give it away?"): the viewer always waits for something

note: the title 'Toyota vs Mercedes: The Car Built to Steal Its Buyers' is a statement: 13 of 20 money Shorts at 160K+ views asked a question ("How much does…", "Why is … so cheap?"); ours with a question had a median of 637 views, name-and-figure statements 456

All 6 facts confirmed on their source pages: Toyota 75-years history (1984 Circle-F start, ~450 prototypes, >3.5M km tests, ~6 years, US Lexus network Sep 1989, Toyota buyers switching to Mercedes/BMW); Jalopnik 11 Jul 2026 ($1B, attributed as 'about'); Motoring Research (LS 400 $35,000, hit 16,000 forecast by end-1989). Verify list met (no outsold claim, $1B attributed). Disclaimer present. Notes: 'at $35,000 a car' is the LS 400 price (ES 250 was cheaper); 'before anyone had heard the name Lexus' is rhetorical (the name was announced before launch).

Re-review: 10s date now reads 1984 (year only, sourced); 40s ending opens on a Lexus showroom sign in Tokyo, so no picture repeats except the loop's Cressida; every still a real place or object with figures on things, no overlaps or cut-offs, 44 s in the 30-55 s band, audio -1.0/-17.6 dB, loop and pick-one ending intact.
